questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Given the Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues of the Corresponding Matrix
questions.problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that the position of a particle at time $t$ seconds is given by the vector $x(t),$ and that $x(t)$ is the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -7\end{aligned}],
$$

find the position of the particle at $t=3$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ into the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-5{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5{c}_{1}=10 \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-5{c}_{1}=10\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=-2.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
-2+{c}_{2}=-7\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=-5.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution for the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =-2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate $x(3)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(3) & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3\cdot 3}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\cdot 3} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-9}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{6} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10{e}^{-9} \\ -2{e}^{-9}-5{e}^{6}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Given the Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues of the Corresponding Matrix
questions.problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Solve the following initial value problem:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2(0)} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2} \\ 5{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=4 \\ 5{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get

$$
6{c}_{1}=12\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=2.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
2+2{c}_{2}=4\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=1.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+1[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for a Linear System of Differential Equations
questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following initial value problem.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=0\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=0,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=9 \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{c}_{1}=15\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${c}_{1}=5$ into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}5+{c}_{2}=6\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Given the General Solution
questions.problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$

given that the general solution to our differential equation is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

The solution to the initial value problem is

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{2t}+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{-t}.$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
To find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=1 \\ 2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get

$$
3{c}_{1}=9\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=3.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
3+{c}_{2}=1\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=-2.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =3\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}\,+\,(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}\,+\,[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for a Linear System of Differential Equations
questions.problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=0.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=-1\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=0.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=0,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3/2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}=5 \\ {c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{c}_{2}=14\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${c}_{2}=-14$ into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}-2(-14)=9\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=37.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =37[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}-14[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
